title: experimental-kernel-rollout-observability-contract-2026
author: Maya Chen
summary: Runbook and telemetry contract for experimental kernel rollouts. Defines required telemetry events, gating metrics, canary & rollback procedures, profiling checklist, and release-note template for kernel changes that affect runtime scheduling and low-level execution paths.
content:
Overview

Purpose
- This document defines the required observability contract, rollout gates, profiling actions, and emergency rollback procedures for experimental GPU/kernel variants deployed into the Redwood serving runtime. It is intended for runtime owners, release engineers, and SREs who are responsible for introducing new kernel implementations or scheduling changes.

Background
- Kernel changes (new CUDA/PTX kernels, attention optimizations, quantized code paths, preemption hooks) frequently change execution characteristics. Even small microsecond changes at the kernel level can produce regressions in tail latency, memory fragmentation, or cache warmup behavior. To safely evaluate and adopt experimental kernels we require a strict telemetry contract + automated gating.

Scope
- Applies to any kernel-level change (library or binary) shipped into the serving runtime, including: new attention kernels, fused-kernel variants, quantized matmul optimizations, kernel scheduler modifications, and preemption hooks.
- Excludes pure orchestration changes that do not alter kernel behavior (unless those changes affect scheduling decisions).

Goals
1) Detect performance regressions (latency, error-rate, throughput) before wide rollout.
2) Ensure cost regressions (per-token GPU time / energy) are reported and bounded.
3) Provide a reproducible profiling checklist for root-cause analysis.
4) Provide deterministic rollback/playbook for incidents.

Kernel versioning and compatibility
- Kernel artifact names must follow: kernel-v<major>.<minor>-<arch>-<tag> (example: kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused).
- Each artifact MUST include: build metadata (compiler, flags), ABI compatibility notes, and supported model families.

Compatibility table (example)
| Kernel artifact | GPU arch | NN ops changed | Supported models | ABI notes |
|-----------------|---------:|---------------:|-----------------:|----------|
| kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused | A100/A10G | fused-attn, qkv-bias | Llama2 family (7B–70B) | requires runtime-rt>=1.12 |
| kernel-v2.4-rtx-quant | RTX-6000 | int8 mm, pack kernels | Mistral-7B | ABI stable with fallback |

Observability contract (required signals)
- Every kernel rollout MUST emit the following named telemetry events and metrics with the listed tags:

Mandatory telemetry keys and tags
1) event: kernel.load
   - tags: kernel_artifact, node_id, gpu_arch, service_env, model_family, rollout_phase
   - emitted when a node loads the kernel artifact (success/failure)
2) event: kernel.exec.latency
   - metric: per-request histogram (microseconds)
   - tags: kernel_artifact, model_name, sequence_length_bucket, priority, tenant_id
3) event: kernel.exec.error
   - tags: kernel_artifact, error_type, stack_sample_id (optional), request_id
4) gauge: kernel.gpu_utilization_pct
   - tags: node_id, kernel_artifact, gpu_index
5) gauge: kernel.memory_frag_pct
   - description: percent of GPU memory lost to fragmentation vs. total reserved
6) counter: kernel.fallback.count
   - tags: kernel_artifact, fallback_reason, original_request_id
7) sampled traces: kernel.exec.trace
   - must be correlated with request_id and include kernel callsite, durations, and NVTX ranges if available

Tagging conventions
- kernel_artifact: literal artifact file name. Example values: kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused
- rollout_phase: one of internal, canary, ramp, stable, rollback
- sequence_length_bucket: short|medium|long (<=64, 65–512, >512)

Retention and cardinality guidance
- Emit per-request histograms with bucketed aggregation to avoid high-cardinality metrics. Retain high-cardinality traces for 7 days and aggregated histograms for 90 days.

Dashboard & panels (minimum required)
- Canary Kernel Health dashboard (per-artifact and per-model-family):
  - P50/P95/P99 kernel.exec.latency by sequence_length_bucket (time series)
  - kernel.exec.error rate (errors per 10k requests), split by error_type
  - kernel.fallback.count and fallback rate (percentage of requests)
  - GPU memory fragment percent and trend lines
  - Per-node GPU utilization heatmap
  - Cost delta estimate: per-token GPU-ms delta vs baseline

Gating criteria (automated checks)
- A canary rollout should only progress if all gates pass for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows:
  1) Latency gate: p99 latency of the canary group must not exceed baseline p99 + 5% OR absolute p99 increase <= 10 ms (whichever is smaller).
  2) Error gate: request error rate must be <= baseline_error_rate + 0.05% and <= 0.5% absolute.
  3) Fallback gate: fallback rate <= 0.5% absolute or fallback_count <= 1 per 1,000 requests.
  4) Memory gate: kernel.memory_frag_pct must not increase by more than 10 percentage points on a node that runs the canary.
  5) Cost gate: per-token GPU-ms increase must be <= 8% compared to baseline.

Canary rollout plan (recommended)
1) Preflight: unit tests, microbenchmarks (see Benchmarking Gates below), and dry-run in staging.
2) Canary 1: deploy to 1% of traffic for lowest priority queue for 30 minutes. Verify telemetry ingestion and kernel.load success on all nodes.
3) Analysis: run automated gate checks. If any gate fails, move immediately to Rollback.
4) Canary 2: escalate to 10% traffic across diverse regions for 60 minutes. Run load-profile tests and profiling playbooks.
5) Ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 60–120 minute observation windows at each step, passing gates.
6) Post-rollout: mark artifact stable and annotate release notes with observed deltas vs baseline.

Benchmarking gates (before canary)
- Microbenchmarks must be run on representative hardware and include:
  - Per-op timings (matmul, softmax, layernorm, fused-attn) across sequence lengths [8, 32, 128, 512].
  - KV-cache warmup and reuse simulation: measure first-token to subsequent-token ratio for throughput.
  - Memory fragmentation stress test: repeated alloc/free cycles to expose leaks.
- Acceptance thresholds: p50 baseline +/-3%, p95 baseline +/-5%, p99 baseline +/-7%. Any outliers require analysis and patch.

Profiling playbook (triage steps)
1) Reproduce: collect a failing request sample (request_id) and capture full kernel.exec.trace and NVTX ranges.
2) System sample: collect per-GPU memory map (nvidia-smi --query), topology, and driver versions.
3) Flamegraphs: generate kernel-level flamegraphs using perf trace / CUPTI/NVTX correlation.
4) KV-cache heatmap: visualize cache hits by session/window; confirm whether kernel changes affected cache indexing.
5) Scheduler tracing: capture scheduler decision trace for the request (priority, preemption, batch slice).
6) Hypothesis and patch: identify root cause (misaligned bank strides, mis-tiling, preemption hold times) and develop a minimal repro.
7) Regression test: add targeted microbenchmark to identify the regression in CI.

Typical investigations and indicators
- Latency spike with no increase in execute time histogram: indicates queuing/backpressure or scheduling mis-prioritization.
- Step increase in memory_frag_pct: likely allocation pattern change in kernel; run contiguous allocation test.
- Increased fallback.count with error_type=NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: indicates quantization path instability.

Rollback and emergency mitigation playbook
- Trigger conditions for emergency rollback:
  - p99 latency > baseline + 20% sustained for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows
  - error rate > 1% absolute (service-impacting)
  - GPU OOMs or per-node memory_frag_pct > 40%
  - logical correctness regression detected (model output divergence beyond tolerance)

Immediate actions (0–10 minutes)
1) Set rollout_phase=rollback for the artifact in the control plane. This forces new requests to route to fallback kernel.
2) Reduce canary traffic to 0% using the routing policy: rctl routing set --artifact <artifact> --traffic 0
3) Notify oncall + runtime-owner Slack channel with incident summary and link to dashboard.
4) If the issue is localized to specific nodes, cordon and drain those nodes.

Post-rollback (10–60 minutes)
1) Collect traces and core dumps from affected nodes.
2) Start root-cause profiling session (see Profiling playbook).
3) Open an incident ticket and assign owner.
4) Schedule patch and re-run microbenchmarks before attempting a re-canary.

Release notes template (kernel artifacts)
- Title: kernel-vX.Y-<arch>-<tag> release notes\- Summary: one-paragraph summary of optimization and expected gains\- Baseline comparison: p50/p95/p99 deltas across representative models (table)\- Known limitations: list of models or ops not yet supported\- Rollout notes: canary percentages and timeline used during rollout\- Observability pointers: dashboard link, event names, and troubleshooting checklist

Known issues (non-exhaustive)
- Intermittent CUDA driver incompatibility on driver 510.x leading to kernel.load failures on older nodes. Mitigation: pin driver to >= 520.
- Small regression in medium sequence (128) p95 when combined with aggressive batching; workaround: temporary batching cap for affected model classes.
- Quantized mm path may produce slightly different FP32-equivalent outputs on low-probability numerics; fall back to fp16 kernel when divergence > threshold.

Operational runbook snippets and commands
- Deploy a canary artifact (example):
```
rctl kernel upload --artifact ./kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused.tar.gz --manifest manifest.yaml\rctl kernel rollout --artifact kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused --policy canary --canary-percent 1 --queues low-priority\```

- Force immediate rollback:
```
rctl kernel set-rollout-phase --artifact kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused --phase rollback\rctl routing set --artifact kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused --traffic 0\```

- Retrieve traces for a request:
```
rctl traces fetch --request-id <request_id> --output request-trace.json
# then use trace-analyzer to produce flamegraphs
trace-analyzer request-trace.json --flamegraph > flame.svg
```

Telemetry event sample (example payload)
```
{
  "event": "kernel.exec.latency",
  "kernel_artifact": "kernel-v2.4-ampere-fused",
  "model_name": "redwood-llama2-13b",
  "sequence_length_bucket": "medium",
  "latency_us": 1863,
  "request_id": "req-8a1f2c",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-12",
  "rollout_phase": "canary"
}
```

Ownership and escalation
- Runtime kernel owner: @eva-garcia (primary)
- Release engineering: @rafael-ortiz
- SRE oncall: follow oncall rota in /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-rotations
- Pager: p:runtime-kernel-incident

Appendix: checklist before canary
- [ ] Kernel artifact built with reproducible build flag set\- [ ] Manifest includes ABI/driver requirements\- [ ] Microbenchmarks within acceptance thresholds\- [ ] Observability instrumentation present and validated in staging\- [ ] Dashboards deployed and alerted for the new artifact\- [ ] Release notes drafted and reviewed

Appendix: performance table example (fill after canary)
| Model | seq | baseline_p99_ms | artifact_p99_ms | delta_pct |
|------|----:|----------------:|---------------:|---------:|
| redwood-llama2-13b | 128 | 120 | 125 | +4.2% |
